title: Customer compliance signal harmonization and triage lattice for enterprise security asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable taxonomy and decision lattice for incoming customer security & compliance requests (questionnaires, SOC2/ISO asks, DPA negotiations, GDPR/data residency questions, HIPAA inquiries) that harmonizes signals across channels (support, AM/SE, sales, legal) and prioritizes response effort, routing, and SLAs.
background: We receive a high volume of diverse compliance asks through multiple channels. Current ad-hoc routing leads to inconsistent SLAs, duplicated work across Legal/Trust/ENG, and missed commitments for high-risk customers. Prior initiatives focused on intake forms and manual scorecards; we need a maintainable taxonomy and triage lattice that can be automated and surfaced in the Console and internal dashboards.
proposed_solution: Design a taxonomy of signals (legal severity, data residency, product impact, contractual request, regulatory risk) with discrete buckets and transformation rules for normalized scoring.

Define a triage lattice: deterministic routing rules (auto-approve info requests, escalate contractual clauses to Legal, route high-risk data residency to Private deployment ops) and human-in-loop checkpoints for borderline scores.
Implement short-term: a middleware scoring engine (serverless) that annotates incoming tickets and emails; long-term: integrate into Console intake flow and partner with Support/AM/SE routing rules.
Expose reasoned decision metadata on each routed ticket (why routed, required evidence, SLA target) and record audit trail for enterprise customers.
Add dashboards/alerts for aging high-severity asks and measure MTTR, SLA compliance, and handoff frequency.
Provide a PRD, decision matrix, and pilot with 3 enterprise customers before wider rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy doc published in Confluence with clear definitions and examples for each signal and bucket.
Triage lattice defined with routing rules, human checkpoints, and fallback behaviors documented.
Middleware PoC deployed that tags incoming asks from Support and Sales with normalized score and recommended route.
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers completed; SLA compliance improved for pilot tickets compared to baseline.
Console intake wireframe that surfaces request reason, score, and estimated SLA is reviewed and approved by Design and Support.
Operational dashboard shows MTTR and open-high-severity counts; alerts created for >48h open high-severity items.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Automation vs accuracy: aggressive automation reduces manual work but risks mis-routing nuanced legal asks — mitigation: conservative thresholds and mandatory human review for legal/contractual flags.
Engineering effort: implementing a scoring engine and Console UI requires cross-team coordination — prioritize middleware PoC first to validate signal mapping.
Customer expectations: standard SLAs may not fit all enterprise contracts — allow per-customer overrides and record exceptions in ticket metadata.
Data sensitivity: storing request metadata must comply with privacy rules (avoid storing customer PII in plain fields) — consult Security and Legal on retention rules.
rollout_plan: Week 1–2: Run stakeholder discovery workshops (Legal, Trust, Support, Sales, SE) and synthesize signal list.
Week 3: Finalize taxonomy and lattice; create Confluence PRD and run tabletop scenarios.
Week 4–6: Build middleware PoC that consumes Support tickets and returns score + route recommendation; smoke test internally.
Week 7–8: Pilot with three enterprise customers (one SOC2-focused, one GDPR/data-residency, one HIPAA-related) with weekly reviews.
Week 9: Iterate on thresholds/rules, prepare Console intake mockups for final sign-off.
Week 10–12: Implement Console integration and dashboards; roll out to broader internal teams with runbook and training.
